seedTerms: Being offered an easy way out

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Open Floor Plan
jokes.joke: I hired an architect who has absolutely no filter. I told him I wanted an open floor plan. He looked at my marriage and said, “You already have one: no boundaries, no support, and every argument echoes through the whole house.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Divorce Lawyer GPS
jokes.joke: I told my divorce lawyer I still love my wife, maybe we can work it out. She didn't even look up from her laptop. She just said, 'That's adorable, sign page twelve.' I said 'don't you have, like, empathy training?' She goes, 'I had it. Now I have a boat.' I've never felt so supported and so sold at the same time.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Renovation Shortcut
seedTermsUsed: Being offered an easy way out
jokes.joke: I hired an architect to redesign my cramped 600-square-foot apartment. He walked in, tapped a wall with his pen, sighed, and offered me the easiest way out: 'Honestly? If you leave a candle burning by these curtains tonight, the insurance payout gets you a much better layout.'

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Brutal Blueprint
jokes.joke: I hired an architect who's brilliant but completely tactless. He walks into my place, looks around for three seconds, and says, "This has real potential... as a controlled demolition site." Then he bills me two hundred bucks for the "vision consult."

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Blueprints
jokes.joke: I tried to help my friend with a tiny zoning issue, because I’m an architect and figured, how hard could it be? Five minutes later I’m in a conference room, accidentally giving legal advice. The lawyer leans over and whispers, “You can’t say any of that.” I said, “Why not? It worked great on my last building.” He said, “Yeah, but buildings don’t sue.”

scores.comment: The boat line is a solid cynical turn, but the joke explicitly introduces empathy as a third seed concept, hurting prompt fit; the closing line also weakens the stronger preceding punchline.
Clear premise and a sharply dark, unexpected architectural solution. The insurance-fire turn lands cleanly, though the construction is more clever than truly explosive.
Clean and stage-ready, but 'controlled demolition' is a fairly predictable insult for a tactless architect. The billing tag adds a useful second beat without making it exceptional.
Strong conversational rhythm and a clean final reversal. 'Buildings don't sue' is an effective punchline, though the premise takes slightly longer than necessary to reach it.
